Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Paris Babe
runners_data.note: Archie Watson filly who has finished in the top six in all five recent turf runs, showing consistent prominent form at 7f on Standard going — Pierre-Louis Jamin takes over and the horse has headgear fitted; solid claims at the top of the prominent group if she avoids early traffic.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed front-runners in this field, Simon Dow's filly sets the pace and has won over 7f on Soft, though her Standard-going form shows no wins from three attempts; 41 days off and a trainer who has only one winner from eight in the past fortnight is slight concern.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this hold-up type for Stuart Williams, whose trainer strike rate of four from 33 in two weeks is reasonable context; her headgear (htp) and consistent record at 7f on Standard make her an obvious beneficiary of a genuinely run race, and a 14-day turnaround suggests she is race-fit.

runners_data.name: Star Mirage
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides this lightly-raced three-year-old who has placed twice from four starts, both at 7f on Good and Standard — only one similar-going run from four suggests Kempton AW experience is limited, but the form of those placed efforts at this trip is solid enough at OR 81.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old is the other confirmed front-runner, carrying top weight for her age, and has form of 2-1 on Soft over 7f; 63 days off is a flag to watch and this is only her third career start, meaning inexperience at handling early pace pressure may be a factor.

runners_data.name: Merry
runners_data.note: James Horton's filly has a strong record at 7f on Standard going with one win and three places from five runs at the track, and was out just seven days ago suggesting sharpness; however, her natural prominent style is squeezed out in this congested field, meaning she is likely to find herself further back than ideal and her chance is tempered by racing out of her preferred position.

runners_data.name: Ribenska
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' four-year-old has a healthy record at 7f on Standard (one win, five places from ten runs in similar going) and returns from 69 days off; Callum Shepherd takes the ride and the headgear note (p) is consistent with recent runs — likely to attempt to get a prominent position but will face stiff competition for that slot in a crowded early field.

runners_data.name: Afraj
runners_data.note: William Buick's presence on this Gosden-trained three-year-old is the headline angle — she won her sole Standard-going start at 7f and has been placed twice at the trip; her trainer sends runners in good form at 6/23 over 14 days and Buick's ability to read a race makes her a credible threat from the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' hold-up filly has placed in two of four runs at 7f on Standard going and is suited by a genuinely run race; Paddy Bradley rides and the headgear (h) is consistent — at OR 75 she is the lowest-rated runner in the field but a strong pace suits her profile and she is not without each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old has placed at 7f on Standard going (2nd from ten similar-going runs) and has a hold-up style that requires a strong pace to exploit; Dylan Hogan takes the ride and at OR 68 she is the lowest-handicapped runner, though a pace-genuine race at Kempton gives her the best chance her rating allows.

races.paceDynamic: Musical Angel and Shushu are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 7f Kempton AW trip, creating a genuinely contested gallop on a Standard to Slow surface that will stretch the field early. Paris Babe, Star Mirage, Ribenska, and Afraj all want prominent positions behind them, meaning the first two furlongs will be crowded and positional battles are likely to generate significant traffic complications two to three furlongs out. This field contains more pace-hungry types than the race shape can accommodate — Musical Angel and Shushu are most likely to actually secure the front two slots, with Merry, who is a natural prominent racer, likely to find herself shuffled into a role that does not suit her. The contested early pace on a surface riding slower than advertised favours hold-up runners who can produce a sustained late run off the tempo set by others — horses with genuine closing ability from midfield or rear will be best positioned to pounce when the front-runners tie up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel and Shushu battle hard for the lead and burn each other out by the turn, gifting the race to horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The contested pace between two genuine front-runners on a Standard to Slow surface creates an honest, draining gallop that leaves the lead pair vulnerable in the final furlong; hold-up and midfield horses with strong finishes get a perfect tow into the race and land their run at the ideal moment.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Leads Controlled
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel or Shushu establishes clear lead authority early and the other fails to go with them, producing a steadier, more controlled pace.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner who dictates from the front on this flat course can control the fractions and produce enough in reserve to hold on; prominent racers who settle just off the leader without having to fight for position benefit most as they get a lead to follow without burning energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Shuffle Benefits Front Two
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion among prominent runners causes interference and bunching two to three furlongs out, allowing the front-runners to steal vital ground unchallenged.
scenarios.body: The mid-race traffic scramble among the four prominent horses disrupts the closers' ability to find clear runs at the crucial stage, letting Musical Angel or Shushu build an unassailable advantage; horses with the cleanest passage from prominent positions gain the most from the chaos around them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Pace Sustainable
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is misjudged as fierce but actually proves sustainable, with the front-runners conserving enough energy to last home.
scenarios.body: On a flat, right-handed Kempton track where experienced front-runners can dictate comfortably, a horse allowed to bowl along uncontested or in a comfortable rhythm can prove very hard to reel in; hold-up horses who need a strong pace to exploit find themselves with insufficient cover to close the gap.

watchPoints.text: Musical Angel and Shushu — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which of the two front-runners blinks first; if neither backs down the pace could be fierce enough to dramatically open the race up for closers.

Paris Babe, Star Mirage, Ribenska, and Afraj all want prominent positions — four horses scrapping for two or three spots creates a genuine risk of bumping and interference between the 6f and 5f marks, potentially costing ground at a crucial stage.

Merry is a genuine prominent racer who is likely to be forced wider and further back than suits her — watch to see if she can recover position on the bend or whether she gets stuck in traffic and her chance evaporates mid-race.

Afraj with William Buick is the key market mover to monitor before the off — Buick's tactical intelligence from a prominent position in a hot pace scenario could make her the one who times her run best of the prominent group.

The Standard to Slow surface is worth noting as slower than typical Standard at Kempton AW — horses carrying heavier weights (Musical Angel 134lbs, Shushu 128lbs) may feel the ground underfoot more acutely in the final furlong if the pace has been genuine throughout.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Gloryous
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has shown willingness to lead but poor recent form (2-6-8-3-2 last five) and zero wins or places from 15 runs on similar going is a serious concern; likely to fight for the lead with Bintknight but may weaken late if that battle is costly.

runners_data.name: Aphrodite Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win on Standard going (1W from 5 similar-going runs) and a solid recent form string showing consistency; 40 days since last run is worth noting but Roger Teal's yard is in decent form at 3/13 over 14 days, and stepping up to 1m4f suits her staying profile.

runners_data.name: Ladykirk
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Jane Chapple-Hyam (3/14 T14), who is the headline angle here; a genuine hold-up type who was placed over 12f on Standard at her last start, and that course and distance form on similar ground is directly relevant to tonight's conditions.

runners_data.name: Bint Kilfrush
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly lightly raced (only three career runs) with a win on Standard going and a 109-day absence that introduces fitness uncertainty; James Tate's yard is 3/17 over 14 days so support should be taken seriously, but the layoff over this trip makes her hard to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style — his five runs on similar going show only 1W1P from 15 — who is mapped to midfield here because the field is heavy with closers; at age 7 and OR 71, his best form has come racing from the rear and being pushed forward may not suit, tempering expectations.

runners_data.name: Bintknight
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old front-runner with two wins from four starts including back-to-back victories at 10f on Good; steps up in trip for the first time to 1m4f tonight and it remains unproven whether he stays, though his honest gallop style could be an asset if he lasts home.

runners_data.name: Affection
runners_data.note: A David Pipe three-year-old with a placed effort over 17f on Good suggesting stamina is not in doubt; a genuine hold-up type in terms of natural style, though the field shape means she is unlikely to get her ideal rear position — that positional compromise, flagged by the style-fit score, mildly dents her chance of producing her best.

runners_data.name: Seacole
runners_data.note: Unknown in terms of running style (rated U) but hg:h (hood) suggests potential temperament management; Ralph Beckett's yard is firing at 6/37 over 14 days, Rossa Ryan takes the ride, and all three career runs show placed form including two seconds, pointing to a consistent filly who should be competitive off the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Gloryous and Bintknight are both confirmed front-runners and will dispute the early lead down the back straight at Kempton, creating a genuinely contested pace over this 1m4f trip on Standard to Slow ground. With two horses actively seeking the front, the gallop should be honest rather than falsely dawdling, which will test stamina in the closing stages on this flat Polytrack circuit. Aphrodite Spirit and Seacole should sit just off the pace in prominent positions, while the hold-up contingent will need to make their ground from further back after a genuine early tempo. This race shape most favours prominent racers who can track the contested lead without being caught up in the scrap, then produce a sustained finish — pure front-runners who lead every metre are at risk of being softened up by each other. Note that the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Big Bear Hug and Affection are true closers but are displaced to midfield in this mapping, and Ladykirk and Bint Kilfrush are the hold-up runners most likely to actually secure a genuine position off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gloryous and Bintknight push each other along from the start, setting an honest gallop that softens both front-runners late.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up through the middle stages, and a prominent tracker like Aphrodite Spirit or Seacole, sitting just off the boil, swoops to pick up the pieces in the final furlong. This shape rewards horses who have the tactical nous to sit second or third and unleash a sustained late run on a flat track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Bintknight or Gloryous establishes a clear lead early and is allowed to dictate a controlled, even gallop without being pressured hard throughout.
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners seizes control, soft-pedals in the middle portion of the race, and holds enough in reserve to repel challengers in the straight on this flat, undemanding circuit. The Standard to Slow conditions slightly favour the horse who conserves energy by setting its own terms rather than being dragged into a war.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is truly strong enough to create a strong final-furlong opportunity for runners coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ladykirk or Bint Kilfrush, sitting in genuine hold-up positions, would benefit if the front two run each other into the ground over the final two furlongs. However, this scenario is tempered by the fact that Big Bear Hug and Affection — the other intended closers — are redistributed to midfield and may not be operating from their ideal berth, reducing the number of true late threats.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between Gloryous and Bintknight is fiercer than expected and both fade dramatically, allowing midfield horses to fill the places en masse.
scenarios.body: A chaotic collapse of the front two opens the race up entirely for horses sitting mid-division, including the redistributed Affection and Big Bear Hug, though both are racing somewhat out of their natural hold-up role which limits their chance of delivering a true finishing burst. The overall likelihood is low because Kempton's flat, undemanding track rarely sees wholesale collapses even in contested-pace races.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Bintknight or Gloryous actually blinks first at the start — whichever of the two front-runners gets a smooth, uncontested lead avoids the pace battle that could cost both of them the race.

Bint Kilfrush returns after 109 days without a run; if she moves freely in the paddock and is supported in the market, the Tate yard fitness angle becomes significant, but a cold market would suggest she needs the run.

Ladykirk with William Buick is the single biggest jockey upgrade in the race — monitor whether Buick pushes her forward to track the leaders rather than riding her as a pure hold-up horse, which would substantially change her chance.

Standard to Slow conditions at Kempton tonight add a stamina premium to this 1m4f trip; runners who have shown stamina at this distance or beyond (Affection's 17f placed run, Ladykirk's 12f form) hold a marginal edge over those unproven at the trip, notably Bintknight stepping up in distance for the first time.

Seacole's headgear (hood) is worth tracking in the parade ring — if she settles cleanly and Rossa Ryan is able to place her just off the pace, her consistent placed form (three runs, three placed efforts) makes her a quiet each-way interest in this shape.

races.name: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Aigeas
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with two wins from five on Standard AW going — the 55-day break is the only concern, but Harry Davies is an excellent young rider for tight finishes and the drop back to 6f after a 7f outing plays perfectly to this profile.

runners_data.name: Wezzeer
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3yo has won on Standard AW and placed twice in four similar-going starts, making the 74-day layoff the key risk; Ray Dawson holds the book well and the prominent style suits if the leaders do their own thing.

runners_data.name: Caviar Cowboy
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent — seven starts on similar going yielding one win and five places — and though James Fanshawe's yard is firing (4/19 T14), the headgear (h) change merits noting as a potential trigger for improvement at this sharp track.

runners_data.name: Society Kiss
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply from 5f to 6f for the first time, which is a significant unknown for a horse that wants to lead — the 79-day break compounds the query, and the trainer's current form (0/1 T14) offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Arry Up
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine on Standard going and has won this course and distance before; the prominent style fits perfectly if the pace is honest and Rod Millman's yard is in form with two recent winners from 19.

runners_data.name: Augustus Gloop
runners_data.note: Fanshawe's second string, and the recent form (2/6f/STA placing) is the one bright light in a disappointing sequence; the hold-up style and 19-day turnaround suggest freshness isn't an issue, but the sim-going record of 1W3P in eight tries is mediocre.

runners_data.name: Manly Fireball
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's runner has front-running claims and a win on this surface, but the sim-going record of 1W6P in nine attempts — and finishing second in the last run — suggests a horse that presses but rarely delivers the killer blow.

runners_data.name: Bintaryana
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over and the horse has placed twice on Standard AW in four tries; the last run (0/6f/STA) is a concern, and without sim-going wins on this precise surface the claims are moderate, though the prominent style means it won't be far away early.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Three wins from 15 on Standard AW — a solid if unspectacular record — and Pat Dobbs is a significant booking; the hold-up style means it needs the anticipated strong pace to set up the closing surge, and recent form alternating wins and defeats (731717) makes it genuinely unpredictable.

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Tongue tie adds an unknown variable, the trainer is winless in 8 recent runners, and the sim-going record of 0W1P in 11 attempts is damning — a confirmed front-runner with no strike rate on this surface who has been out of the frame in all five recent runs.

runners_data.name: Slay Queen
runners_data.note: No similar-going runs listed and a string of double-figure finishes on Good ground offer no encouragement; the hold-up style needs a race set up that this field could theoretically provide, but there is insufficient evidence of quality to recommend.

runners_data.name: From The Hip
runners_data.note: Two wins on Standard AW from eight similar-going starts make this the most proven course-and-distance winner in the field; the 79-day break is the only serious worry, and the prominent style from a low draw should allow Tyler Heard to slot into a clean position.

races.paceDynamic: Society Kiss, Manly Fireball, and Kolkata Knight all want to lead, ensuring this 6f Kempton AW contest is run at a strong, relentless gallop from the outset with no tactical conservatism — the Standard To Slow going will compound the stamina demands on those setting the pace. The front three will battle for supremacy into the first furlong, creating early friction and likely burning each other out before halfway, with Society Kiss (stepping up significantly in trip from 5f) and Kolkata Knight (poor recent form, 0W1P on similar going) both looking vulnerable to fade. Prominent horses like Wezzeer, Caviar Cowboy, Arry Up, and Bintaryana face genuine traffic danger as five runners converge on that second/third rank — those who can't find a clean run 2f out will be cooked. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina and the ability to finish powerfully through a fatigued field, with Aigeas, King Of Chaos, and Augustus Gloop the natural beneficiaries of a strongly-run pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out setting a fierce early gallop and the field fractures from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Society Kiss, Manly Fireball and Kolkata Knight competing aggressively for the lead creates a genuine pace collapse scenario, leaving the closing furlong entirely to horses arriving from off the pace with energy to spare. Hold-up runners who have settled behind the carnage and find a clean passage are the primary beneficiaries of this dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse avoids the early pace war by sitting just off the leaders in second or third and pounces at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A runner like Wezzeer or Arry Up, who slots in smoothly behind the duelling front-runners without expending early energy, can time a run to hit the front with 1f remaining before the hold-up horses fully wind up. This shape rewards horses that are genuinely comfortable racing prominently on Kempton's straight AW track and have class to sustain a challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Society Kiss or Manly Fireball secures a clear lead uncontested within the opening furlong while rivals check each other.
scenarios.body: Should one leader establish undisputed control and set a controlled rather than suicidal gallop, the pace becomes less punishing and a front-runner with enough stamina can simply hold on. Society Kiss has course-winning form at Kempton and could exploit this if Kolkata Knight breaks slowly and Manly Fireball gets outpaced early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Moderate, Field Bunched
scenarios.trigger: If early speed burns out quickly but hold-up horses get blocked in traffic and prominent horses dominate the straight in a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: The five prominent-positioned runners create a wall of horses in the straight, with hold-up types struggling to find daylight through a tightly bunched field racing below expected pace. Horses with tactical versatility who can race one position forward of their natural station benefit most in this messy, compressed scenario.

watchPoints.text: Society Kiss, Manly Fireball, and Kolkata Knight — three confirmed front-runners battling for the same strip of rail in the opening 2f creates the risk of contact, checking, or early pace explosion that could compromise all three and several runners directly behind them.

Prominent congestion at the 2-3f marker is severe with five runners (Wezzeer, Caviar Cowboy, Arry Up, Bintaryana, From The Hip) all targeting the same racing position — watch for traffic snarls and horses being forced wide or checked at the critical stage.

Kolkata Knight's tongue tie (first-time application flagged by hg:t) is a live market mover watch — if it settles the horse and allows a more controlled front-running display it changes the pace scenario entirely from chaos to controlled lead.

Aigeas returns from 55 days off for Oliver Cole's yard which has not had a winner from 10 runners in the past 14 days — a quiet trainer strike rate means this is a fitness question that should be monitored in the betting before committing.

Standard To Slow going has been confirmed for this race across multiple reports — fractionally slower than true Standard conditions will marginally extend finishing times and could expose any horse that has only won on faster Standard surfaces.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Charlie Fellowes who won over 12f at Goodwood on good — the step back to AW Standard to Slow at Kempton could be workable, but his true closer's style needs a proper gallop that this pace shape is unlikely to deliver; only 6 days since last run which is sharp.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up juvenile whose one win came on soft ground, and his sim-going record on comparable surfaces reads 1 from 6 with zero wins and zero places — the AW Standard to Slow here is a concern; Jason Watson rides and he'll need something to go wrong for the leaders.

runners_data.name: Cosmo Brown
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's three-year-old has hit the frame over 12f on good going twice but has been consistently beaten and his hold-up style leaves him at the mercy of a race that is shaping as a slow-pace tactical affair; Callum Shepherd takes over but the scenario doesn't suit.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's gelding won over 10f on good and has placed over 10f twice, but his sim-going record on comparable conditions is 2 from 8 with no wins or places — 39 days off and his natural position at the rear of the field is problematic when the pace is set by one lone, unhurried horse.

runners_data.name: Hot Silk
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's filly has placed on this surface twice and boasts a sim-going record of 3 from 6 with one place, giving her the strongest AW credentials among the redistributed runners; she is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position, and Harry Vigors's 5lb claim is an asset if she gets cover.

runners_data.name: Semper Femina
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's filly has placed at 12f on good and holds one sim-going place from six attempts — she is a natural hold-up type who finds herself depicted in midfield purely because the field is packed with closers, and the slow pace is unlikely to generate the fractions she needs to finish off.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: William Buick's big booking for Ollie Sangster attracts the eye immediately, but Amrum's 63-day absence and a sim-going record of 1 from 6 with no wins or places temper enthusiasm; a true hold-up runner by nature, the lack of pace makes it hard to see how even Buick conjures a winning move.

runners_data.name: Far Far Out
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's lightly-raced three-year-old is flagged as fading in finishes and has only three runs to his name — he is a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield depiction, and the combination of a modest pace, a fade flag, and 58 days off makes this a difficult assignment; William Carson's fitness angle worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly is the race's lone pace-setter and Cieren Fallon can dictate entirely on his own terms — her AW sim-going form shows 2 from 5 with one place and her last run over 12f on Standard produced a runner-up finish, giving her legitimate claims if allowed to control the gallop; the style-fit note reflects she's a prominent rather than true front-runner, but she'll likely lead by default.

runners_data.name: Lord Mayor
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's stayer has placed five times in his last five starts across Standard and Standard to Slow AW surfaces, giving him the strongest course-and-going profile in the race — PJ McDonald partners a hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield, but his consistency at this track and trip makes him a prime candidate if the bunched finish scenario materialises; 197 days off is the only concern.

runners_data.name: Tinsel
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's gelding won over 10f on Standard AW and has placed on the same surface — a sim-going record of 4 from 8 with one win and one place is solid, and though he is a natural closer pushed into the midfield depiction, his AW winning form and tactical speed give him a realistic chance in this pace shape; 30 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Cospicua
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly has won twice on this surface, including at 12f on Standard, and her sim-going record of 8 from 9 with two wins and two places is the standout AW statistic in the race — a natural hold-up runner depicted in midfield due to field congestion, but her course-and-going record and Ray Dawson's experience at Kempton keep her firmly in the picture.

races.paceDynamic: Evening Fades is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-horse field at 1m4f on a Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface, meaning she can dictate an uncontested, unhurried gallop from the front without any genuine pace rival to press her. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly comprised of hold-up horses — Hot Silk, Semper Femina, Amrum, Far Far Out, Lord Mayor, Tinsel, and Cospicua are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply not enough natural pace in this field for them to occupy their preferred rear positions meaningfully. With Evening Fades able to control tempo, this shapes as a slowly-run, tactical affair where those immediately behind her in a compressed midfield bunch will be best placed, as the lack of true pace is unlikely to produce the strong sustained gallop that genuine closers need to pick horses off from the rear. The race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can sit close to the moderate pace and produce a finishing kick — true hold-up horses who need a strong tempo to be wound up from the back will find conditions against them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evening Fades Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades dictates a moderate, uncontested pace and the compressed field fails to produce a significant sustained gallop.
scenarios.body: Evening Fades drifts along setting a comfortable rhythm with Cieren Fallon barely needing to push, and horses sitting prominently or in the forward half of the midfield bunch get the clearest run into the straight; the Standard to Slow surface rewards those who conserve energy close to the pace rather than those making up ground from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the midfield compresses entirely and several horses challenge simultaneously in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no real gallop set, the race becomes a sprint from 2f out and horses with tactical speed sitting mid-division — ideally those with course form on the AW — find themselves ideally placed as Evening Fades is swallowed up inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades increases tempo mid-race and creates a stronger-than-expected gallop, allowing genuine hold-up horses to finish off powerfully.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would stretch the field and allow horses like Traveling Man or Relentless Hero to pick off tiring rivals in the straight, though this scenario is discounted because the redistributed hold-up types are not running in their true position and a faster pace is the least likely outcome with one lone pace-setter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades sets a crawl and the race degenerates into a cavalry charge from 3f out with no horse getting a clear run.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish from a very slow pace suits the horse with most tactical adaptability and a clean draw or position, though this shape is difficult to predict and depends on Fallon misjudging the tempo entirely.

watchPoints.text: Evening Fades and Cieren Fallon — if she is allowed to stride into a lead of 3-4 lengths unchallenged before the home turn, the race is effectively hers to give away and no hold-up horse in this field is well-placed to reel her in.

Lord Mayor's 197-day absence is a significant flag — PJ McDonald will need to judge this fit enough to do himself justice over 1m4f on a Standard to Slow surface, and a blow-up late in the race would open the door considerably.

William Buick on Amrum will attract significant market support but Amrum's 63-day layoff and lack of any sim-going success make this a speculative booking; watch whether the market drifts pre-race as a guide to stable confidence.

Cospicua's AW form record is conspicuously strong (8 from 9 in similar going) and James Tate's yard is 3 from 17 in the 14-day window — watch whether Ray Dawson attempts to put her closer to the pace than her natural style suggests to exploit the slow gallop.

The field of 12 with 11 natural hold-up horses and one front-runner means the straight at Kempton could see a wall of horses challenging simultaneously — watch for horses drawn widest who may get the cleanest unobstructed passage up the outside.
